status: V01K insufficient: freeze reproduced; Gate A unaccepted
scope: muted 2K-workload trial of V01K (masked-preflight fix), one live capture of the frozen device

baseline_before_trial.note: clean post-reboot baseline; no startup FIFO0->11 excursion this boot

human_report: SECS advanced correctly against a stopwatch, so the diagnostic clock was valid for this run.
Raising LFO speed: at about speed 256/512 it started crashing and lagged extremely.
Cable pulled, waited 30 s: still completely frozen.

capture.pi_engine_line: fifo min 89 max 89 target 96 under 29295 | blocks 0 | cpu c1/c2/c3 0.0% | sysex 13166 | to-host sent 263195 B 10977 msgs fail 1

findings.masked_preflight_race_is_not_the_cause: With the authoritative in-mask preflight shipped, the device still freezes and stays frozen after the cable is pulled. The race was a real defect worth fixing, but it is not what produces this hang.
findings.freeze_occurs_at_lower_speed: The freeze occurred at about speed 256/512 rather than only at 2K, i.e. still above the 64/48 slow-but-responsive band, so the trigger scales with update rate as before.
findings.all_device_counters_stop_together: rx/seq/block/timer/sends identical across three samples 30 s apart, so this is a stop, not gradual saturation; the remote emitter dies with the device.
findings.worker_elapsed_badly_inflated: Worker elapsed is 74% of elapsed time at only ~410 sends/s, versus ~25% at ~816 sends/s in the original G dense capture (~160-340 us/send). Per-send worker time here is roughly 1.8 ms. Unexplained, and worse than the pre-fix image, so it must be resolved before another flash.
findings.deferral_semantics_risk: This change made a zero-length send a deferral rather than a fault. A native queue that stops draining now yields unbounded retries instead of a fail-closed retire. That is a behaviour change introduced by this fix and is a plausible contributor to the inflated worker elapsed; it needs a bounded retry/retire rule.
findings.no_hardware_fault: Pi stayed alive, 54 C, no throttling or undervoltage; the frozen device is simply no longer sending.

not_established: Which native wait, if any, is entered
Whether the RX/ACK interrupt path participates
Whether the deferral change interacts with the freeze
next: Bound the deferral: after a bounded number of consecutive refusals or a bounded age, treat it as a fault and retire, restoring fail-closed behaviour.
Then address the RX/ACK interrupt path: the Pi ACKs every snapshot, so the receive handler runs at the same rate and parses frames plus wakes inside interrupt context.
Do not flash again until the worker-elapsed inflation is explained offline.
limits: No on-device trace of the failing program counter: the remote emitter stops with the device
Derived milliseconds assume the 132MHz diagnostic timer, which is not proven to be the CPU clock
Exact LFO numeric settings were stepped by hand to ~256/512, not read back
Muted trial: says nothing about audible quality
